summary: Enforce cross-trap invariants tying Proxy reports to the complete fixed own-property/prototype/extensibility state of a non-extensible target.

target.notes: Use the JavaScript object-model runtime. Proxy semantics require trap lookup, handler calls, target internal methods, revocation checks, and invariant enforcement.

semantics.extensibility: isExtensible trap must equal target; successful preventExtensions requires target actually non-extensible
semantics.prototype: getPrototypeOf/setPrototypeOf cannot report a different prototype once target is non-extensible
semantics.properties: existing own properties cannot be hidden and new own properties/keys cannot be fabricated where invariants forbid it
semantics.own_keys: must contain exactly target own keys when target is non-extensible

caveats: Do not model Proxy as a plain C# decorator or Dictionary wrapper; observable internal-method interception and invariants must be preserved.
references: ECMAScript 2026 §6.1.7.3 Invariants of the Essential Internal Methods

tests.name: delete cannot claim existing property deleted
tests.input: const t={x:1};Object.preventExtensions(t);const p=new Proxy(t,{deleteProperty(){return true}});try{Reflect.deleteProperty(p,'x')}catch(e){console.log(e instanceof TypeError)}

tests.name: ownKeys cannot omit property on non-extensible target
tests.input: const t={x:1};Object.preventExtensions(t);const p=new Proxy(t,{ownKeys(){return []}});try{Reflect.ownKeys(p)}catch(e){console.log(e instanceof TypeError)}
